ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. (80) of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, as amended by Law No. (36) of 2014, and its Executive Regulations promulgated by Prime Ministerial Decree No. (1135) of 2002; Companies Law No. (159) of 1981, as amended, imposing the mandatory beneficial-ownership register administered by the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI); Investment Law No. (72) of 2017; and Central Bank of Egypt AML/CFT Regulations issued under Law No. (88) of 2003.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Good Standing of the Ultimate Foreign Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry of the jurisdiction of origin of the parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (public notary certification, Ministry of Foreign Affairs certification in the country of origin, then Egyptian Embassy/Consulate legalization)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the Egyptian incorporation counsel and local shareholder representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public Notary in the jurisdiction of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution of the foreign corporate shareholder authorizing formation of the Egyptian LLC and approving the initial UBO list
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or chairman of the foreign entity, certified before a notary public

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Ultimate Beneficial Owner Declaration and Certified Ownership Structure Chart identifying all natural persons holding 25% or more
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or licensed attorney attesting identity and nationality of each UBO

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Passport Copies and Proof of Residential Address of each Director, Authorized Signatory, and 25% or more Beneficial Owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public Notary in the country of nationality or residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter evidencing source of funds and standing of the sponsoring shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Correspondent commercial bank of the sponsoring shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization with authenticated bank signature

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-filing screening of every shareholder, director, authorized signatory and 25% plus UBO against: (i) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; (ii) the OFAC SDN List; (iii) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (iv) Egyptian national terrorist-designation and prohibition lists published by the Egyptian Money Laundering Combating Unit (EMLCU); and (v) domestic and foreign PEP registers maintained under Law No. (80) of 2002, including family members and close associates. Any PEP or sanctions indication requires senior-management approval, enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification and ongoing transaction monitoring for at least 12 months; screening evidence must be retained for the statutory minimum of five years and produced to the EMLCU upon request.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Invest in Egypt integrated online One-Stop Shop (gafi.gov.eg) and the Commercial Registration Office system under the Commercial Registration Law No. (34) of 1976
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be filed in Arabic for the Commercial Register; a Latin/English transliteration is recorded simultaneously and must be an exact phonetic equivalent approved by GAFI in the incorporation certificate. The name must reflect the company object, i.e., manufacture of health-monitoring smartwatches and smart wearables, must include the LLC corporate indicia as required, and may not be identical or deceptively similar to any existing registered company name or trademark.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Insurance, Securities, or Financial Intermediation (requires prior CBE/FRA licensing)
Military, Defense, Police, Security, Intelligence, Nuclear
National, General, Sovereign, Public, Governmental (requires ministerial consent)
Egypt, Arab, Arab Republic, Egyptian (restricted for foreign-controlled companies unless expressly authorized)
Islamic, Christian, and other religious names or references to religious figures
Names contrary to public order, registered trademarks, or historical and symbolic personalities

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (Arts. 102-125 for LLCs), as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018 and Law No. 1 of 2019 (electronic formation); Executive Regulations per GAFI (Investment Law No. 72 of 2017); Commercial Registry practices under the Ministry of Trade and Industry
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Commercial Registry and Corporate Registration Department (with the electronic Nafeza portal)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application on Nafeza / GAFI commercial registry electronic form together with the Notarial Articles of Association (Contract of Formation) and capital deposit certificate
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies for LLCs; founders determine subscribed capital in the Articles. The capital must be deposited into a blocked temporary bank escrow account at a licensed Egyptian bank, and the bank's capital-deposit certificate must be submitted to GAFI prior to issuance of the Commercial Registry certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers having adopted the Articles of Association of [Company Name] S.A.R.L. (LLC), the formation is hereby ratified and the Company is declared duly established under Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended; and RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company shall be established at the leased premises identified in the Articles; and RESOLVED FURTHER, that the issued share capital shall be fully subscribed by the founding members, deposited to the temporary bank account, and the deposit certificate delivered to GAFI; and RESOLVED FURTHER, that the following officers are appointed, namely Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Compliance Officer, each authorized to execute regulatory filings, open bank accounts, and issue statutory declarations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Economic Activity Pre-Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop and Online Services Portal (www.gafi.gov.eg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply in Arabic and transliterated English for the company's commercial name via GAFI's e-service. Select ISIC 2652 (manufacture of health monitoring smartwatches) as the primary activity and confirm it is permitted. Obtain the name reservation certificate and filing reference. Non-resident founders must attach consularized powers of attorney for remote filing.
required_dossiers: Proposed Arabic and English company name
Passport copies of each founding member
Notarized and consularized Power of Attorney for each absent founder
Description of the smart wearable manufacturing activity tied to ISIC 2652
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for conflict, file an administrative objection with the GAFI Name Committee and refile with a modified transliterated name; the Committee generally issues a decision within two business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization and Execution of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Justice Certified Notary Public, in coordination with GAFI Legal Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Have the founding members or their attorneys execute the Arabic Articles of Association before a notary. The notary verifies identity, legal capacity, and the lawful nature of the object clauses, and certifies the execution. Obtain notarial certificate copies for registry filing.
required_dossiers: GAFI name reservation certificate
Draft Articles of Association in Arabic
Valid national ID cards or passports
Powers of attorney for non-resident signatories
Lease promise or executed lease for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary concludes any clause is unlawful, the founders execute a corrective addendum and the notary re-certifies the Articles; no additional GAFI fee is incurred when the correction is made before registry filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Deposit and Bank Escrow Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Egyptian commercial bank (corporate accounts unit)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary incorporation account in the name of the company and deposit the subscribed capital. Obtain the bank's capital deposit certificate and the account opening documentation. The account remains blocked until the company obtains the Commercial Registry certificate, after which funds are released and the certificate is cancelled or updated.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarized Articles of Association
Passport / identity documents of signatories and ultimate beneficial owners
Bank KYC and source-of-funds declaration
Name reservation certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank's AML/KYC unit requests further evidence, provide a corporate group diagram and bank statements for source of funds; the deposit certificate is reissued immediately upon clearance and completion of the account documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Filing with GAFI and Commercial Registry Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation application on Nafeza by attaching the notarized Articles, bank capital deposit certificate, lease contract, name approval, and payment receipts. Upon GAFI approval and fee settlement, the Commercial Registry certificate (C.R.) is issued. The company acquires legal personality from the date of the registry entry.
required_dossiers: Name reservation certificate
Original notarized Articles of Association
Bank capital deposit certificate
Certified copy of registered office lease
GAFI incorporation application and fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond on Nafeza within ten working days and correct the flagged item; re-submission of the same transaction preserves the filing date. If the application is formally rejected, refer the matter to the GAFI Dispute Resolution Committee for a ruling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inaugural Board Resolution and Officer Notifications
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Corporate Registry (post-incorporation filing window) and company seat
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the constituent meeting of the subscribing members, adopt the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution, and keep original minutes with the share register at the registered office. File the appointment of the legal representatives and the registered address with GAFI within the statutory notification window using the registry form prescribed after C.R. issuance.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registry certificate
Minutes of the constituent meeting including the board resolution
Written acceptance letters from CEO, CFO, and Compliance Officer
Evidence of qualifying registered office premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry returns the notification because of signature deficiencies, attach the notarized minutes and refile; late submission incurs a minimal statutory late fee. Submit a corrective memorandum and pay the fee to maintain good standing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT, and Social Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) and the National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to ETA for a Tax Card and VAT registration within the statutory deadline from C.R. issuance; provide payroll declarations to NOSS once employees are hired. Complete e-invoicing setup and obtain the required digital signature certificate for electronic filing. Keep all registration certificates at the registered office for industrial licensing reference.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registry certificate
Articles of Association
Bank account certificate and capital deposit release letter
Legal representative identification and powers
Board resolution appointing the CFO as tax manager
Employee payroll schedule for NOSS Form 1
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ETA issues an error query, respond within the deadline via ETA's digital platform; obtain a temporary registration slip if the Tax Card is delayed. Correct payroll imbalances through NOSS e-service and resubmit the affected declaration to avoid assessments.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA) - الهيئة العامة للتنمية الصناعية, Ministry of Trade and Industry
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Industrial Operating License (رخصة التشغيل الصناعي) and Industrial Registration Certificate issued under Law No. 15 of 2017 on Industrial Licensing

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) - جهاز شؤون البيئة
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B - Rapid Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA Form B): smart wearable electronics assembly, printed circuit board soldering, and lithium battery pack integration are moderate-impact activities requiring an EIA Form B screening before IDA license issuance; a full Category C EIA is not mandatory unless electroplating or hazardous waste recovery is added.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: treated industrial rinse water must comply with the sewer discharge limits in Law No. 48 of 1982 and the Executive Regulations of Environment Law No. 4 of 1994 (as amended by Law No. 9 of 2009), including suspended solids and heavy metal ceilings; no chromium, nickel or cyanide above detection thresholds. Air emissions: soldering fume extraction systems must keep VOC concentrations below 50 mg/m3 in the breathing zone and stack VOC discharges below 20 mg/m3; ambient air levels to be verified by a licensed EEAA consultant. Hazardous waste: spent lithium batteries, solder dross and waste resins must be segregated, labeled and transported only via an EEAA-licensed hazardous waste contractor with signed manifests. Noise must not exceed the occupational limit of 85 dB(A) over an 8-hour shift.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense Clearance: fire safety certificate from the General Administration of Civil Defense (Ministry of Interior) covering automatic fire suppression, exit routes, and electrical compliance for the electronics production floor. Structural Clearance: certified engineering inspection confirming that floor loading capacities accommodate manufacturing machinery and battery storage areas. Occupational Clearance: workplace safety and health approval from the Ministry of Manpower under Manpower Law No. 12 of 2003, including ventilation, personal protective equipment, and electrical safety for surface-mount and soldering operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax and Customs Authority (ETCA), Official Portal: https://etca.gov.eg/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities register with the ETCA to obtain a Tax Registration Number (TRN). The procedure requires submission of commercial registration certificate, company incorporation documents, ownership structure, address proof, and passport copies via the ETCA online portal, followed by document verification and issuance of the TRN within 30 days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available in Egypt. Default entity-level taxation applies to LLCs. Hybrid mismatch rules are governed by the Income Tax Law for cross-border transactions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time e-invoicing through the ETCA Fiscalization System requiring digital stamping, QR codes on invoices, and API integration for data exchange with the authority; fiscal clearance is mandatory before any transaction.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to exports of goods and services to non-residents. Eligibility requires the place of supply to be outside Egypt, goods to physically leave the country, and supporting export documentation.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent zero-rating claims attract penalties up to 200% of the VAT amount, interest charges, and potential criminal prosecution. Retrospective audits result in clawback of zero-rated amounts with backdated assessments.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a managed-float exchange-rate regime. EGP is generally convertible for current-account transactions, including trade settlements and profit/dividend remittances, subject to supporting documentation and clearance of any tax obligations. Capital-account transactions, such as foreign-direct-equity injection and repatriation of paid-in capital, are routed exclusively through licensed Egyptian banks and require prior or contemporaneous registration with GAFI and, in certain cases, CBE approval. Dividend/profit remittance is permitted without prior CBE approval, provided audited financial statements, a tax clearance stamp or declaration, and the statutory corporate formalities are completed. Actual convertibility can be constrained by temporary USD liquidity tightness, so treasury planning must factor in the CBE's foreign-currency auction and interbank order flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBE foreign-exchange regulations, export proceeds must be received and credited to a licensed Egyptian bank account within 90 days from the date of the export declaration issued by Egyptian Customs. The exporter may apply for an extension of up to a total of 360 days on trade-backed, case-by-case grounds. The mandatory conversion ratio is 0%: since the November 2016 EGP flotation, export proceeds may be retained in foreign currency in the exporter's local bank account. However, the full amount of the export-related receipts must be repatriated into the Egyptian banking system within the statutory or extended timeline; retaining funds abroad or using offshore digital EMI accounts as a permanent repository is non-compliant.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Foreign-Currency Account (used as the initial capital inflow escrow account pending GAFI registration)
Capital Escrow Account in EGP and a USD current/operational account for trade settlements
Operational USD/EGP treasury account with dedicated trade-finance and hedging lines

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Qatar National Bank Al Ahli (QNB ALAHLI)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account for receivables collection and vendor payments

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI platforms (e.g., Airwallex, Payoneer, Wise Business) have medium viability for collecting USD/EUR export receivables as a supplementary treasury front-end, but they have low viability as a primary treasury rail inside Egypt. CBE regulations do not license these institutions as banks or authorize them to clear through Egyptian payment infrastructure; they cannot open local EGP IBANs, issue EGP-denominated settlement, or act as the repatriation account for export proceeds. All export proceeds must finally land in a licensed Egyptian bank within the 90-day repatriation window. Therefore, the compliant design is to use an offshore EMI only for preliminary invoicing/concentration and then to wire the net proceeds via SWIFT MT103 into the Egyptian operational account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, tier-1 Egyptian banks mandate a physical presence of at least one natural-person director/authorized signatory at a local branch during initial KYC onboarding for a non-resident or foreign-owned LLC. Remote opening is not a standard CBE-sanctioned procedure for corporate accounts in the establishment phase, though a bank may allow a video-enhanced filing if all corporate documents are notarized, legalized at the Egyptian embassy, and accompanied by a power of attorney. Subsequent treasury operations may be executed through digital banking once the signatory mandate and sample signature are on file.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO with unclear source of wealth or tax-residency footprint
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copy, home-jurisdiction proof of address, two independent professional reference letters, audited group financial statements, a documented source-of-wealth narrative, and a complete uninterrupted ownership-chain registry extract.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of demonstrable substance or physical office at the registered Egyptian address
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered lease or ownership deed, GAFI/commercial registry extract, an Egyptian corporate legal opinion, third party contracts with local suppliers, payroll or outsourced staff services, and utility bills matching the address.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Exposure through supply-chain relationships to high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due diligence questionnaires, transactional counterparty declarations, beneficial-ownership registry extracts, commercially reasonable pricing evidence, import/export insurance certificates, and a written trade-compliance policy.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (1) Register the investment with GAFI under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 to create a recognized inward-capital file; (2) hold a board resolution designating the specific Egyptian bank account as the capital-receipt account; (3) instruct the sending bank to issue a SWIFT MT103 with a GAFI file reference and the Egypt CBE purpose code for 'Foreign Direct Investment — New Capital Participation'; (4) ensure the beneficiary bank receives the wire into the foreign-currency account and issues a certificate of inflow or foreign-currency declaration; (5) after receipt, file the capital-inflow statement with GAFI and CBE so that future dividend remittance and capital repatriation will be honoured. For in-kind capital (machinery, inventory), obtain a CBE-attested valuation certificate and a commercial import declaration before the contribution is counted as paid-in capital.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For importing components used in smart-watch manufacturing, the treasury clears outbound payments through two principal rails: (a) SWIFT MT103 for open-account or prepayment trade settlements, using Egyptian CBE purpose code for 'trade settlement' and attaching a proforma invoice, LC reference, or purchase contract; and (b) commercial documentary Letters of Credit (sight or usance) opened through the Egyptian bank for high-value or contractually secured supplies. All outbound trade payments are subject to CBE-backed documentary examination to verify that the commercial invoice, bill of lading, packing list, and insurance certificate align with the declared transaction. For export receipts, the corresponding inbound rail is a SWIFT MT103 from the foreign buyer into the Egyptian receiving account; the treasury must verify the CIB/e-code or account syntax to prevent rejection.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forward contract — permitted for hedging a contracted underlying trade, repatriation, or dividend obligation, typically with a tenor of up to 12 months, offered by licensed Egyptian banks against WBR (interbank) rates.
Onshore FX swap — used to convert temporary USD/EGP cash mismatches on capital flows and working-capital cycles, subject to underlying exposure documentation and bank credit approval.

Offshore non-deliverable forward (NDF) — accessible to non-resident counterparties and, through licensed Egyptian banks, as a mirror structure for residents where deliverability is not required by the CBE.

Cross-currency option or swap — permissible for large approved USD/EGP transactions where the bank's market-risk committee documents the hedged item as a confirmed trade/capital flow; plain-vanilla FX options on EGP are not generally permitted onshore.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (juridical persons form), accompanied by audited financial statements and tax adjustment schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year LLC, no later than 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing and late payment penalties accrue at 2% per month on tax due, capped at 100% of the tax; continued non-filing enables discretionary assessment, bank attachment, and tax evasion prosecution under Law 91/2005.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements (balance sheet, income statement, management report) deposited with the commercial register after partners' approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry under the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after fiscal year-end after the annual partners' meeting; calendar-year LLCs generally file by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file in two consecutive years can trigger administrative strike-off and referral to liquidation, and may result in fines against managers and non-renewal of the commercial registration certificate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual contract inventory and related-party disclosure attached to the corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed together with the annual corporate income tax return no later than 30 April for calendar-year taxpayers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incomplete disclosure exposes the LLC to revised assessments for omitted transactions, transfer-pricing adjustments, and accuracy penalties computed on additional tax.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory for all active Egyptian LLCs. Companies Law 159/1981 requires appointment of at least one licensed auditor, including where the LLC has more than ten partners; Income Tax Law 91/2005 requires audited financial statements to accompany the corporate income tax return. No turnover-based statutory audit exemption applies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), substantially converged with IFRS; supplementary IFRS consolidation may be prepared for foreign parent reporting. Tax accounting begins with EAS profit before statutory adjustments.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under AML Law 80/2002 as amended, the LLC must maintain a beneficial ownership register on site. Share transfers are documented in writing and become effective upon entry in the Register of Members; any change in shareholding must be reported to GAFI within 15 days. At each annual partners' meeting, the manager presents a reconciliation of share transfers and confirms that the UBO register matches the Register of Members and the audited financial statements; this confirmation is minuted and retained in the statutory minute book.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$800 – US$2,200 per annum (registered office and in-country corporate secretarial agent in Cairo / Greater Cairo)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$1,500 – US$4,000 per annum for an SME smart-watch and wearables OEM under Egyptian Accounting Standards

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying free-zone projects may receive a 0% corporate income tax rate on export profits under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017. Deductions and investment incentives are also available for manufacturing equipment, R&D expenditure, and regional headquarter activities, but the general 22.5% headline rate applies to an Egyptian LLC manufacturing smart watches and fitness wearables.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Egyptian Corporate/Company Income Tax Return Form No. 10 (EIT Return), filed via the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) electronic filing portal at https://www.etax.gov.eg.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within four (4) months after the close of the fiscal year. For a calendar-year manufacturing LLC, the return is due by 30 April of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identity: legal name of the LLC, Tax Identification Number (TIN), Egyptian registered address, commercial register number, fiscal year start and end dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Egyptian branch or permanent establishment (PE) registration details; a non-resident without a PE is not required to file Form No. 10 and is instead subject to source withholding taxes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit before tax: total revenue from smart-watch and fitness-wearable sales, related components, after-sales services, and foreign exchange gains, less cost of goods sold and deductible operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An Egyptian PE must report only Egypt-source revenues and margins attributable to the PE under the arm's length principle; group-level revenues or offshore sales processed directly by the parent must be excluded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back and non-deductible items: provisions, entertainment expenditure exceeding the statutory cap, penalties, excessive intercompany charges, and expenses not supported by valid tax invoices or accounting records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recharges from the foreign parent must be supported by a transfer pricing file and demonstrate actual service beneFit; otherwise the Egyptian Tax Authority may disallow them as hidden profit distributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory deductions and incentives: free-zone exempt income, investment incentives, capital allowances, and tax loss carryforward claims limited to five (5) years from the loss year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident parent cannot claim its home-country losses against Egyptian PE income; only losses recorded in the Egyptian tax account may be offset.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax computation: taxable income at 22.5% corporate income tax, less tax credits, provisional tax payments, and withholding tax credits, resulting in final balance payable or refund claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withholding tax credits on Egypt-source income are available to the PE; treaty relief outside the return, e.g., reduced dividend WHT, must be invoked via the ETA treaty-relief procedure and supported by a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration, signatures, and attached schedules: audited financial statements, related-party transaction schedule, transfer pricing Local File / Master File, and any free-zone or investment-incentive certifications.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident taxpayers claiming treaty or PE benefits must attach the TRC, substance evidence, and arm's length documentation; failure to attach these schedules will attract penalties and trigger audit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and failure to submit accurate returns trigger a monthly delay surcharge of 2% of the unpaid tax and administrative fines. Deliberate misreporting or tax evasion may lead to fines, confiscation, travel bans, and imprisonment for responsible officers.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a Double Taxation Agreement (DTA) reduced rate, the non-resident beneficial owner must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the home jurisdiction, provide a certified Arabic translation (with legalization or apostille if required), submit the treaty-relief application to the Egyptian Tax Authority International Taxation Office before or at the time of dividend distribution, and disclose the ultimate beneficial owner. If statutory withholding was already applied, the non-resident may claim a refund through the ETA within the statutory limitation period, typically five years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax on interest and royalties paid to non-residents is 20%. Depending on the applicable DTA, the reduced rates generally range from 5% to 15% for interest and 10% to 20% for royalties, subject to limitation-on-benefits and economic substance requirements.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 10,000,000 aggregate related-party transactions in the tax year triggers the mandatory Local File; higher group revenue and transaction thresholds apply for Master File and Country-by-Country reporting under the Egyptian Tax Authority regulations.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt applies substance-over-form and general anti-abuse principles under Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005 and Investment Law No. 72 of 2017. Free-zone and treaty benefits are denied where an Egyptian LLC lacks real business premises, personnel, accounting substance, or genuine decision-making; a shell company booking smart-watch sales without actual manufacturing or distribution substance will be re-characterized by the ETA.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating revenue from smart-watch exports, using dual bookkeeping, falsifying invoices, concealing bank accounts, or overstating deductions on the Form No. 10 return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005: imprisonment of three (3) to five (5) years, fines up to the tax evaded, confiscation of concealed assets, plus monthly delay surcharge of 2% on unpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who participate in or authorize fraudulent filings may be held jointly and severally liable for the corporation's tax debt. The ETA may pierce the corporate veil, issue travel bans, and remit the case for criminal imprisonment sanctions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Cross-border sales between the Egyptian LLC and a non-resident parent or OEM supplier without an arm's length price; failure to prepare Local File / Master File above the EGP 10 million threshold; excessive management fees; or artificial profit stripping through purchase of electronic components.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA re-characterization of taxable income to the arm's length result, additional tax at 22.5% plus 2% monthly delay surcharge, and administrative fines for incomplete or absent TP documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving non-arm's length transactions without a valid TP study risk personal assessment if the arrangement is found to be an illegal advantage or a misuse of corporate form. Financial sanctions, civil restitution, and director-level criminal referral may follow.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Default on Outbound Dividends / Royalties / Interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: An Egyptian LLC distributes dividends to a non-resident shareholder, or pays royalties or interest to a foreign affiliate, without deducting and remitting the statutory 10% dividend WHT or 20% interest/royalty WHT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer remains legally liable for the un-withheld tax; the ETA assesses full tax recovery, a monthly delay surcharge, and fines for non-remittance. Repeated violation may trigger criminal prosecution for willful non-payment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly direct payments abroad without withholding or who conceal the beneficial recipient may be jointly and severally liable for the unpaid withholding tax. Travel restrictions and imprisonment can be imposed for fraudulent evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Egyptian LLC as a letterbox or conduit for smart-watch trade with no real production, employees, premises, or economic functions, while moving funds through Swift/TT or LC payment rails to conceal ultimate beneficial ownership or launder proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Anti-money-laundering penalties under Law No. 80 of 2002, including imprisonment, fines up to EGP 1,000,000, freezing of bank accounts, and confiscation of funds tied to illegal cross-border transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate veil piercing for AML offenders: directors, shareholders, and beneficial owners may be personally liable, subjected to travel bans, asset freezes, and imprisonment in addition to civil restitution of laundering proceeds.
